messages:
amy: Heads-up: early-morning EU-W3 promo spike led to near-OOM behavior on several GPU hosts and a short throttling cascade. Putting raw notes here for the post-incident writeup.
ben: saw alerts ~00:05 UTC, GPU util jumped to ~99% for multiple shards, several pods started evicting caches.
maria: can you paste short metric snapshot? curious about network egress and kube evictions.
amy: metric snapshot from 00:03-00:18 (highlights):
```
00:03 - sudden RPS burst +52% vs baseline (batch infer)
00:04 - GPU util 95-100% on euw3-shard-[2,3,5]
00:06 - node mem pressure crossed 90% on 4 nodes -> kube eviction of cache dirs
00:07 - autoscaler increased replicas but cool-down delayed action ~140s
00:10 - concurrent model shard pulls spiked, GRPC retries increased -> throttling
```
sam: infra logs show many distinct prefixes causing KV-cache footprint to balloon. Prefetch path attempted parallel model pulls which saturated local NIC snd queues.
ops-runbook-bot: Incident INC-2026-0502-EUW3-CAPACITY created. Runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/capacity
ben: quick repro in staging that mirrored memory blowout when we simulate many unique prefixes:
```
# staging stress: 60 concurrent varied-prefix requests
for i in {1..60}; do curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/generate -d '{"prompt":"random ${i}","prefix":"uid-${i}"}' &
done
```
maria: proposed root causes: 1) forecast underestimated weekend promo uplift (~40-55%) for EU-W3, 2) autoscaler policies have conservative cool-downs and step sizes, 3) caching model assumed high prefix reuse which failed for this workload, 4) simultaneous shard pulls caused transient socket exhaustion and GRPC backpressure.
amy: impact: short SLO blip (p95 increased ~600ms), customer-facing errors 500/503 for ~12 minutes for some routes, two elevated support tickets.
sam: cost: spilled into on-demand GPUs + overtime ops run for ~1.5h. Early estimate extra infra cost ~$3.1k.
maria: overnight mitigations applied: manual capacity bump + temporary headroom, disabled long-tail cache retention for new prefixes, rolled a smaller quantized fallback model for high-latency requests.
ben: actions & owners:
- forecasting: add promo-aware signals + weekend multiplier (owner: maria)
- autoscaler: add OOM/reactive fast-path to bypass cool-down and allow rapid scale-up (owner: devops)
- cache: change eviction to size-weighted LRU and enforce per-prefix caps (owner: sam)
- runtime: stagger model shard pulls during scale-up and prefetch on new node attach (owner: eng-runtime)
ops-runbook-bot: Logged tasks: #2410 forecast updates, #2411 autoscaler fast-path, #2412 cache policy change, #2413 shard prefetching.
maria: short-term recommendation: increase EU-W3 reserved headroom by 30% for 72h, tighten GPU mem alert to 80% (P0), and run synthetic burst test in CI simulating many unique prefixes. Finance aware of cost delta.
finance: noted: 30% headroom estimated cost +$6.5k/week; prefer predictable availability over repeated incidents.
amy: additional telemetry we need: concurrent model-shard-pulls per node, GRPC retry spike metric, per-prefix cache occupancy. Please add these to dashboards.
sam: also saw transient socket exhaustion traces (~30s) on nodes during the peak; adding ephemeral-socket-mgmt ticket.
devops-bot: Action items assigned and scheduled.
ben: I'll draft the postmortem sections (timeline, root causes, mitigations, cost impact, rollout plan) and circulate for review tomorrow.
amy: thanks team. keeping thread open for any extra logs or short notes.
